Oliver: Quick follow-up from the handshake-replay RFC — we left the replay -> ownership mapping fuzzy. if a replayed billing event arrives but the original provenance was never persisted, what should the ingest do? do we assign credits conservatively, hold for manual review, or try to reconstruct ownership heuristically?
Maya: I think conservative default: mark as replayed and don't auto-charge until we can stitch a provenance pointer. but we should try heuristics first (fingerprint match + time window). :thinking_face:
Liam: +1 on heuristics first. propose idempotency key = "fingerprint||ingest_instance||sequence". that gives us deterministic dedupe across retries and replay attempts. downside: cross-region replays may use different ingest_instance ids.
Sam: For cross-region we can canonicalize ingest_instance to a region id (e.g., us-west-1) and fallback to a null suffix if unknown. also: charging windows matter — if replay lands outside billing window, we can't just retro-charge without audit trail. suggest flagging replayed events to the billing-recon pipeline instead of main ledger.
Tara: Observability ask: every replay should carry origin_trace_id pointing at the original request (if present). and a claim_source enum so downstream knows whether this came from handshake, ingester-repair, or replay job. e.g., claim_source: handshake|repair|replay. makes rules easier in recon.
Oliver: Agreed. concrete flow idea: 1) ingest accepts replayed event but sets claim_status=\"pending_recon\" if provenance missing, attaches replay_meta. 2) quick heuristics attempt stitch; if heuristic confidence >= 0.9 auto-claim, else route to async recon with human review.
Maya: That confidence threshold needs to be tunable per-customer (some tenants want conservative). config should live on the tenant profile + global overrides.
Liam: Implementation detail: heuristics service should be idempotent and expose a explain string for audit. e.g., \"matched fingerprint+session_id (0.94)\" so accounting can show why we auto-claimed.
Sam: For billing correctness: always emit a bilateral audit_event when a replay causes a state change: {type: \"replay-claim-apply\", decision: \"auto|manual|defer\", explanation, prior_state, new_state, operator}. these go to long-term cold storage for compliance.
Tara: +1. Also we need a path to revert. if a later audit disproves the heuristic, we should emit compensating events, not mutate history silently. compensation should increment a separate metric (compensations_count) for SLA accounting.
ingest-bot: replay-job-processor started for tenant=acme-corp, job_id=job-20240315-7a9f. processing 412 events.
Oliver: Quick event schema proposal (small snippet):
```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "fingerprint": "sha256(...)",
  "claim_source": "replay",
  "origin_trace_id": "trace-xxxx",
  "replay_meta": { "original_ingest_ts": "ts", "replay_job_id": "job-..." },
  "claim_status": "pending_recon"
}
```
Liam: That shape looks good. Add optional original_handshake_id and original_region fields. and ensure event_id is stable across retries.
Maya: We should also include a small TTL on replay_meta to avoid infinite manual queues (e.g., escalate after 30d).
Sam: For runtime, I propose two fast paths: fast-accept (auto-claim when heuristics succeed) and slow-path (enqueue to recon). metric names: meter.replay.auto_claims, meter.replay.manual_queue_depth, meter.replay.compensations.
Tara: UX: console should show replayed events with a dedicated filter and an explain panel showing heuristic reasoning & links to evidence (raw event, origin trace). helpful for finance audits.
Oliver: Action items: @Maya draft tenant-config PR for confidence thresholds and escalation TTL. @Liam sketch heuristics service API (idempotent evaluate + explain). @Sam add the audit_event contract and metrics. @Tara mock the console panel. I'll put a short RFC addendum with the flow and schema.
Maya: on it, will ping once PR is up.
Liam: I'll prototype evaluate endpoint this week.
Sam: I'll add audit contract to the billing schema repo and wire a test.
Tara: I'll produce a console mock and link it here.
